articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.description: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.content: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine.
